title.value: Latent Space Representations of Neural Algorithmic Reasoners
title.justification: The title is explicitly mentioned at the top of the paper.
title.quote: Latent Space Representations of Neural Algorithmic Reasoners

analysis.description: This paper explores the latent space structures induced by Graph Neural Networks (GNNs) when executing algorithms in neural algorithmic reasoning tasks. It identifies weaknesses in the typical GNN architectures and proposes improvements using softmax aggregation and latent space decay to tackle these issues. The proposed changes are validated on the CLRS-30 benchmark, improving the performance on a majority of algorithms.

type.justification: The paper involves empirical evaluation of proposed methods on benchmark datasets, examining GNN architectures and their performance.
type.quote: We show that these changes lead to improvements on the majority of algorithms in the standard CLRS-30 benchmark when using the state-of-the-art Triplet-GMPNN processor.

name.justification: The paper focuses on the use of GNN architectures for executing algorithms and understanding the latent spaces in neural algorithmic reasoning.
name.quote: A typical approach is to rely on Graph Neural Network (GNN) architectures, which encode inputs in high-dimensional latent spaces that are repeatedly transformed during the execution of the algorithm.

name.justification: The paper is centered around neural models simulating classical algorithms using neural network architectures.
name.quote: Neural Algorithmic Reasoning (NAR) is a research area focused on designing neural architectures that can reliably capture classical computation.

name.justification: The analysis and understanding of latent spaces in neural algorithmic reasoning are central themes of this paper.
name.quote: We perform a detailed analysis of the structure of the latent space induced by the GNN when executing algorithms.

name.justification: It is used as the state-of-the-art processor on which improvements are demonstrated.
name.quote: We use Triplet-GMPNN [8] as the NAR processor for evaluation, as it is currently state-of-the-art on CLRS-30.
